newsitem.title: USA: Late muni OSs are not just bond dealers problem.
newsitem.headline: Late muni OSs are not just bond dealers problem.

text.p: Securities regulators are examining whether municiapl broker-dealers are failing to file official bond statements on time, but issuers and other market participants also have some soul searching to do on the matter, the MSRB's chairman said Tuesday.
"There's two sides to that story," Roger Hayes, managing director of NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc and MSRB chairman, said at a Government Finance Officers Association panel session here.

"Lots of times it turns out that dealers have some very legitimate problems in getting official statements filed" on time with the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board, Hayes said. He said occasionally, for instance, issuers may not send the documents to dealers on time.
Rule-G-36 requires municipal bond dealers to file official statements with the board's electronic repository within certain timeframes.

Underwriters of primary offerings must file a copy with MSRB one day after getting the OS from the issuer and no later than 10 business days after any final agreement to purchase, offer or sell the securities.

The Bond Buyer reported last week that the National Association of Securities Dealers and Securities and Exchange Commission are conducting "major examinations" to target dealers that have failed to comply with Rule G-36 deadlines.
Hayes said, "There's a lot going on, and its very difficult to honestly sort it all out as to where the real problem lies (in) getting information in investors' hands on a timely basis."
Christopher Taylor, MSRB executive director, said SEC's 1994 muni disclosure rule requires dealers and issuers to have a written contract to produce an OS.
"We then get it from the dealer and the dealer is also supposed to give it to the customer. What we are finding is that that process, from beginning to end, is not working," Taylor said.
